items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I sat in on a lot of his sound tracks for MGM and the way he rehearsed the band

ctx.x: Yes, he was doing some TV things.

Yes, TV things, and it involved, you know, when you cut your sound tracks, like for 105 musicians, one of those things. I was fortunate enough to be in on some things that the great Russian composer and arranger, Lennie Hayton, Lynn Haven, you know, Lena Horne's husband -- I sat in on a lot of his sound tracks for MGM and the way he rehearsed the band, you know, and all, and I knew he was well versed in all those things. And that was the first time that I had seen a big band rehearse with the big sheets in front…

And I asked Lennie Benny one thing. This is very interesting. And this was -- with politics going on. I guess I can say this, but I says, 'Lennie, Benny,' I said, 'Why is it so necessary to have four first violins or, second four violins?' He says, 'You really want to know?' I said, 'Why, sure.'
